subject: Deployment segmentation criteria & next steps
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya@financio.com>, Arjun Rao <arjun.rao@financio.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Jun 2028 12:15:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment segmentation criteria & next steps

Hi Priya / Arjun —

Thanks again for the 30-minute call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum:

Recap from our discussion (high level)
- Financio’s top concern: strong separation of customer data and proof of custody (no shared persistent storage, auditable access).
- Options considered: Hosted API (fastest to ship), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs, single-tenant compute but hosted control plane), Private (VPC or on-prem private control plane).
- Specific asks you raised: customer-managed KMS, ability to restrict egress from compute nodes, retention/audit log windows, and whether Redwood control plane must be inside Financio network for compliance.

What I believe you want to confirm next:
1) Whether Dedicated capacity meets your data segregation/Risk Appetite if the control plane is hosted by Redwood.
2) Whether Private VPC (customer VPC peering + private control plane) or on-prem is required to meet regulatory needs.
3) Checklist items you’ll use to make the decision (KMS, SSO, audit retention, network egress).

Proposed next steps
- Please share the security checklist you mentioned during the call (I can loop in engineering once we have it).
- Technical deep-dive with our infra lead (Ben) and security PM (Marcus) to go over KMS options, network flows, and auditability — 60 minutes.
- I’ll prepare a short decision criteria doc that maps your checklist to our deployment options so you can share with your compliance team.

Available slots for the deep-dive: Mon 6/12 10:00-11:00 PT or Tue 6/13 14:00-15:00 PT. Which works best?

Attachments: placeholder for your checklist (please attach) — I’ll attach our Private offering one-pager immediately after you send the checklist.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0178

From: Priya Desai <priya@financio.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Arjun Rao <arjun.rao@financio.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Jun 2028 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment segmentation criteria & next steps

Thanks Monica — appreciated. Attaching our security checklist (FIN-Sec-Checklist_v3.pdf) for your reference. A few clarifying questions from our side before we pull the compliance team in:

- On customer-managed KMS: can Redwood integrate with an external KMS (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault) such that keys are not exportable and encryption is enforced at rest and in transit?
- For Dedicated capacity: we heard that compute can be single-tenant, but does any metadata or telemetry flow to Redwood’s hosted control plane? Is there a way to disable that or keep it in our VPC?
- For Private VPC vs on-prem: what are the practical differences from a compliance perspective (data egress, control plane ownership, patching)?
- Audit logs: can you provide retention SLAs and support delivery of logs to our SIEM (Splunk) via a secure push or S3 export?

We’re not certain the compliance group will accept a hosted control plane. If control-plane-in-customer-network is a hard requirement, on-prem or fully private control plane will probably be needed.

Please loop in Ben / Marcus for the technical session. Preferred slot: Tue 6/13 14:00-15:00 PT.

Attachment: FIN-Sec-Checklist_v3.pdf (see attached)

Best,
Priya Desai
Head of Security Operations
Financio
priya@financio.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Jun 2028 15:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: prep notes for Financio deep-dive

Monica / Marcus — quick internal note before the call on Tue:

Short answers we should be prepared to share
- KMS: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS (AWS/Azure) where keys never leave the customer account; we can document the envelope encryption flow and key policies. This satisfies the non-exportable key requirement.
- Dedicated capacity: compute nodes can be single-tenant and diskless for model shards (we keep ephemeral caches in memory only). However, the default Dedicated control plane (autoscaling decisions, billing, routing) lives in Redwood-hosted control plane. We can limit telemetry but cannot move the control plane into the customer network without Private.
- Private VPC: offers peering and private control plane option (control plane can be deployed into customer VPC under our Private offering) — meets strong compliance asks short of full air-gap.
- On-prem/private: for customers who require control plane in their network or air-gapped operation, we can provide an on-prem package; this will add operational lift and lead time.
- Audit logs: we can push logs to customer S3 or Splunk; standard retention is 90 days by default, can extend to 1 year as an enterprise configuration.

Proposed messaging for the call:
1) If Financio requires customer-owned control plane or air-gap -> propose Private (VPC or on-prem) and outline lead time & operational handoffs.
2) If requirement is "no persisted customer data on shared storage" and customer-controlled KMS + log export -> Dedicated capacity can be acceptable but needs formal confirmation on telemetry policy and contract language to limit control-plane obligations.

I’ll prepare a short diagram of network flows for the deep-dive and a checklist mapping to their FIN-Sec-Checklist_v3.

-Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Deployment segmentation criteria & next steps

Priya — thanks for the checklist and for confirming Tue 6/13 14:00 PT for the technical deep-dive. Quick answers to the items you raised below; we’ll expand on each during the call and follow up with docs:

1) Customer-managed KMS
- Yes — for Redwood Private we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault). Keys remain in your tenant and we use envelope encryption; we’ll share a KMS integration diagram and required IAM roles during the call.

2) Dedicated capacity and control-plane/telemetry
- Dedicated provides single-tenant compute. By default some telemetry for routing and health is retained in Redwood’s control plane for reliability/rollbacks. If your policy requires zero hosted control-plane telemetry, Dedicated alone is not sufficient; we must move to Private. We can, however, negotiate contract language to explicitly limit telemetry collected and provide attestations.

3) Private VPC vs On-prem
- Private VPC: control plane can be deployed into your cloud VPC (we run the control plane in your account or via a private peering model) — minimal egress and standard for customers who need strong network isolation but still want Redwood to manage ops.
- On-prem: full control plane in your data center/air-gap; highest compliance but longer lead time and more customer ops.

4) Audit logs & SIEM
- We can export audit logs to S3 and/or push to Splunk over a secure channel; retention can be increased to 12 months for enterprise contracts.

Next steps
- Technical deep-dive Tue 6/13 14:00 PT — Ben and Marcus will walk network flows and KMS setup.
- I will share a short decision-criteria worksheet that maps your checklist to the three deployment paths by EOD Mon 6/12.
- If after the deep-dive Financio’s compliance team requires control-plane-in-customer-network, we will move the conversation to Private (VPC or on-prem) and I will connect you with our Private deployment PM to discuss timelines and SOW.
